clue.text: Maybe note is me?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be otherwise, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical item wonders whether it might be a note itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'Maybe' rearranges NOTE IS ME, and the step from the note 'me' (mi) up to 'fa' is exactly a semitone.
explanation.definitionFit: A half step in the scale, such as mi to fa, is the musical interval meant, loosely called a note.

clue.text: Inward-looking solvers ordered masks

indicators.note: to mask is to cover over, so the word for ordered closes around and conceals the solvers

parts.note: to order people about is to ... them, giving ...
the setter addresses solvers as 'you', archaically ye

explanation.surface: Introspective puzzlers were told to put on disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross-eyed, with eyes turned in towards the nose, is a squint that literally looks inward.

clue.text: More understanding issue in Europe?

definitions.meaning: comparative of kind: more sympathetic and gentle
issue means offspring, and the German word for children is this one

explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word for sympathetic; separately the German noun for children, issue in one European language.

clue.text: See 12
Person climbing down depends on people flying up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: depends on means relies on, giving relies
BA is British Airways, an airline that flies people

explanation.surface: Someone descending trusts the folk passing overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying up' looks like a description of the people, but 'up' reverses everything, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone descending a rock face on a rope in a controlled slide is a rappeller, the person meant.

clue.text: Dog left to bite bespectacled nebbish, one nowadays missing a lead?

indicators.note: biting takes something between the jaws, so the dog-and-left letters close around the nebbish

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a dog
Woody Allen, the glasses-wearing film-maker famous for playing timid, hapless characters

explanation.surface: A dog is let loose to nip a nerdy man in glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: A nebbish is a meek, ineffectual man, Woody Allen's screen persona. The definition plays on a dog's lead: a fallen idol no longer leads, having lost a following.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero who has lost public adoration no longer holds the leading position once enjoyed, a pun on a dog's lead.

clue.text: Dish Chinese lawyer served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the letters upward, so the pieces are backwards

parts.note: Sino- is the prefix meaning Chinese
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A plate of Chinese food brought to a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like food beside 'served', but it is the slang sense of a handsome man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, and the mythological beautiful youth names any handsome man.

clue.text: Call on falling bombs more, in opening shot

indicators.note: the word for a shot is opened up so other letters go inside it

parts.note: to have a go is to have a shot

indicators.note: bombs as a verb means explodes or goes badly, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A cry as more bombs fall in the first salvo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombs' is a verb doing the anagram, not the falling bombs of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroopers traditionally shout this Apache chief's name as they jump from the aircraft.

clue.text: See 26
Infestation of children, it seems?

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Children seem to be carrying lice.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across childrEN IT Seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice eggs in the hair are the classic infestation among schoolchildren, so the word stands for an outbreak of them.

clue.text: It's perilous to cross immoral leader invested in Greenland after meltdown

indicators.note: invested means placed within, so the leading letter goes into the other letters
a meltdown breaks a thing down, so the letters of the island are rearranged
a leader is the first, so the opening letter of immoral is taken

explanation.surface: A wicked ruler installed in Greenland as its ice melts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after meltdown' rearranges GREENLAND into DANGERLNE, and 'invested in' puts I, the first letter from 'leader' of 'immoral', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary whose crossing brings hazard is one where risk begins, a perilous threshold.

clue.text: His words exhaustive, deprive our leader of power

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter it, depriving it of potency
Boris Johnson was the British Prime Minister, the leader in power, when this was published

explanation.surface: A demand to strip the Prime Minister of authority, whose speeches go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 English dictionary, a work of words that is exhaustive. In 2019 Boris Johnson was Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century lexicographer's dictionary set out the language's vocabulary at exhaustive length.

clue.text: Ill wind arising, innumerable common criminals initially punching dandy, officer on the way?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upward, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: a crude word for breaking wind

indicators.note: punching into something drives a hole in it, so the initials go inside the dandy

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man vain about clothes

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the next words are taken

explanation.surface: A bad smell rises as countless criminals hit a fancy dresser before an officer arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill wind' is a crude joke for breaking wind; 'arising' reverses it because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer who directs vehicles and deals with motoring offences works on the road.

clue.text: Hypocrisy in Lesson One doubly affected

indicators.note: affected means put on or altered, so these letters are rearranged
doubly means the following letter is used twice

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy in the first lesson twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives II from One; 'affected' rearranges LESSON with II.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarminess, an unctuous manner suggesting false sincerity, is the figurative sense meant, a near synonym for hypocrisy.

clue.text: Jumble sale's ending after dash to fill car

indicators.note: after puts the ending letter behind the car-and-dash letters
filling means going inside, so the dash goes into the car

parts.note: MG is a British make of car
dash in the sense of flair or verve is elan

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of the word for the charity sale

explanation.surface: At a jumble sale's close, someone dashes to load the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' looks like part of 'jumble sale' but is the definition; a jumble sale is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture or medley of different things is a jumble, a synonym taken from French.

clue.text: Moon named Calypso's core, eg rocky

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaken, so the letters are rearranged
the core of the nymph's seven-letter name is its central letter

explanation.surface: A rocky moon named after the heart of Calypso, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Calypso is also a moon of Saturn, which sharpens the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest satellite of Jupiter, named after Zeus's cupbearer, is an example of a moon.

clue.text: See 25
Very old houses set to be demolished — that's a blow

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so very old's word holds the other letters

parts.note: early means from long ago, very old as in early history

indicators.note: demolishing knocks a thing apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ancient homes are slated for demolition, which is a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' looks like a setback, but it is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind coming from the east is a kind of breeze, and blow is a casual word for a wind.

clue.text: English chap not entirely into American broad beans

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the shortened chap goes inside the broad

parts.note: in American slang a broad, a woman, is a dame

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An Englishman barely slips into broad beans in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broad beans' looks like one item, but 'broad' is American slang for a woman, DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Young green soybeans served in their pods are a type of beans, popular in Japanese cooking.

clue.text: Political party made to pay, shut up

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for the Conservative party
a person made to pay a penalty is fined

explanation.surface: A political party is forced to pay up and goes quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' looks like a call to silence, but here it means locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone kept within limits or imprisoned is shut up, as in a cell.

clue.text: Republican impressed by topless model too

indicators.note: pressed into, so the Republican letter is placed inside the model's word
topless in a down clue means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a lovely is a glamorous woman, such as a model

explanation.surface: A Republican is taken with a model who goes topless as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes L from LOVELY to leave OVELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively means to an excessive degree, as in 'too keen', so the adverb sense matches.

clue.text: Refinement in Chopin's words?

definitions.meaning: Chopin was born in Poland, so his words were in his native language

explanation.definitionFit: Sophistication or finish is one sense; separately the national language of Poland, which the composer spoke.

clue.text: Clear case, unpacking middle

indicators.note: unpacking takes out the contents, here the central letter

parts.note: in medicine a case is a patient

explanation.surface: An obvious example, with its contents unpacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvious, as in a plain lie, is the adjective sense, a synonym for clear.

clue.text: Nicely shortened business degree secured by force — a walkover for entrants?

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: well means nicely, as in done well
Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: held in by, so the degree is put inside the force

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A smart business degree obtained by force makes things easy for newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkover' looks like an easy win, but entrants literally walk over this.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat at the entrance is literally walked over by visitors arriving.

clue.text: See 2
Show skinned peach

indicators.note: skinning removes the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a peach is a very attractive person, a sexpot

explanation.surface: Display a peach with its skin removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' looks like fruit, but it is slang for a gorgeous person.
explanation.definitionFit: A large public exhibition or trade fair is a show.

clue.text: Old player in game breaking bank

indicators.note: breaking into means going inside, so the game goes inside the bank

parts.note: Lloyds is a major British high-street bank
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: An old gambler plays a game while robbing a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Lloyd Bridges was an American actor, star of Sea Hunt and Airplane!
explanation.definitionFit: The late American actor was a performer of the past, and player is a word for an actor.

clue.text: Go in the corner of this room, pal having nobody to play with

definitions.text: Go in the corner of this

indicators.note: playing with something fiddles with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lonely friend in the corner of a room with nobody to play with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb but is the corner square where Monopoly players start.
explanation.definitionFit: The property-trading board game has its starting square in one corner of the playing surface.
